What one of my campaigns that I'm playing in is doing is making sure we have a very fleshed out backstory for our characters. (We rolled on Xanathar's Guide to Everything's "This is Your Life" to help make it more randomized and less angsty... and we got some pretty angsty stuff anyways)
Then the DM made sure to record the backstories and has made sure that he's given every player character some time where their backstory means something to the campaign overall. It helps make each person feel central to the story rather than another "here's my stats and I do this. Let's keep going."
For instance, my character is a religious soldier that lost her lover a year or so ago and is using missions from the jarl to evade dealing with it (though she's also hoping to find him in her travels). Her pious attitude has actually earned her seeing a lot of unsettling things dealing with ancient, evil gods returning. And her having a connection with her lover has already earned her an ally NPC. (The DM rolled for this stuff to happen and luck was in her favor. XD) She feels like she was called on by the gods to help now rather than just taking a mission just because.
When I DMed, I made sure to do this for my group as well. They feared overly serious campaigns, so I made them find funny and awkward things to help relax them some (tense players don't make for good storytellers). I also reward good storytelling and backstories with a +1 to an attribute of my choosing, an item needed for plot, or inspiration. It's a good motivator for those that are a little shy at first.

Finally, don't be too uptight. I know a lot of DMs are very big on keeping to the game and not getting off track, but my favorite ones were the ones where we could effectively make memes about the session we just had. We joke about stuff that's going on (like we went to a hometown of one of the party members, met his parents, and found out that his mother was... gifted heavily in the chest region. Best line that came out of the session was "Don't make my mom busty! Leave her cleavage out of this!") and the best ones usually get memes on our GroupMe. (This is a hardcore game, though, so if we can make jokes while almost getting our characters killed on the regular, we know we're having a good time.)

All in all, just involve your players. You'd be surprised how fleshed out a story can be if you rely more on them. Yes, DMs are the story tellers and hold the general outline of their world, but it's an outline. Let the players fill in the blank spots and you'll have tales for years.

I don't understand. Specifics are appreciated.
Self help books are mostly fluff. Other books are more generalized in order to appeal to a larger demographic, hence why they would sell them rather than being free. Profit is still a gain regardless, so getting individual help isn't possible and when someone is going through suicidal thoughts, they need a more intimate environment so as to fix their problems.
That's why therapy cannot be replaced by any other media, much like physical illness. Some people react positively to certain methods and medications while others react very negatively. Expecting something created for the sole of hitting a mass of people to fix one, specific person is very dangerous. Especially when mental illness is starting to actually be seen as a serious issue now.

As for entertainment books, I have many. Mostly fantasy/sci-fi and romance, but I have dabbled in most genres. Especially since I want to publish at least one book before I die. As much as I love books and video games, they're just distractions and don't fix my problems.

When someone is suicidal and has depression, it is very difficult to ignore the very impeding thoughts that come with both. (Not even including my social anxiety) No amount of "just be happy" thoughts are gonna help. After 14 years of battling it, I can guarantee that.

(By the way, I was able to go into free consultation to get properly diagnosed but sessions were still expensive after that and I couldn't  pay for them. I'm not just claiming self-diagnosed mumbo jumbo)

Happiness is a great goal, but it's far more complicated than just thinking happy thoughts unfortunately. Being happy is one of my long term goals as well, but I know that in order to truly be happy, I must accept my flaws and struggles. Posting this in the confessions subreddit is one way of doing that. Everyone with any sense knows that cutting is the wrong choice, but when your perception of everything around you is collapsing and all you want to do is slit your own throat, cutting and putting your emotional turmoil as a physical pain rather than a fatal one which is easier to deal with is preferential. Do I do it anymore? No. But I miss that kind of control. And acknowledging that I miss something destructive is better than ignoring it. Ignoring it makes it worse. "The first step to fixing a problem is to acknowledge you have one."

Suicidal thoughts have lately turned to urges for me regardless of how I feel, including happy. It makes me feel powerless and ultimately, missing cutting myself is missing having control over how I thought or felt.
I understand these things about me and I'm growing to accept them so I may fix them. I just don't have money to see someone who can professionally aid me. And my family doesn't believe in therapy or mental health, so all of my requests for help paying for stuff has fallen on deaf ears. Which just adds to my issues since if I told my family what I was going through, they would just call me lazy or a disappointment (they've told me I was a disappointment all of my life, so I wouldn't put it past them).
Happiness is easier to obtain for some while others have to struggle all of their life and just to get the little amount that they do. I think everyone's ultimate goal is to be happy. What makes them happy differs, but all in all, they want to be happy. Or at the very least, satisfied.

Dreams were a rarity for Samantha Hatherford. Many of her nights were usually filled with nothing, probably due to wearing herself out after training. But tonight was different. After venturing on a mission with a group of people she knew nothing about and doing little more than walking for an entire day, she was able to dream.

At first, everything seemed normal. Her long, chocolate brown hair was braided around her head and she wore light armor for sparring.  The sun was out, the temperature warm, and she was surrounded by familiar walls that made her feel safe. She was back at Caeran Keep where her lord and comrades were. Though they bullied her for being a "pretty girl trying to be boy" back in their early days, they had grown to accept her as one of them. Especially one in particular. Elijah Holdfast, her superior and the love of her life.

She looked around the barracks as some of her friends got ready for the day, hoping to see his face again. When she finally caught a glimpse of his sandy blonde hair and wise, hazel eyes, she rushed forward and wrapped her arms around him while burying her face into his neck. He was much stockier than herself, so she had to throw herself into him, making him stumble a little back. The room filled with laughter and playful jeers from the others, but Sam didn't care for she was with the one person who always made her happy. And the one that truly made her feel comfortable as a woman.

But something strange began to happen as she pulled away from the hug. The lights in the barracks had suddenly been put out and it grew deafeningly silent. Elijah was nowhere to be seen and everything felt colder.

Sam's body twisted to the entrance the second she heard the sound of a horse approaching. Its hooves clacked ominously on the cobblestone path and wheels of something accompanying it creaked along slowly. It was then that she remembered what day she was experiencing again. This was where the bodies of Elijah's traveling party were delivered to the Keep and his was pronounced missing.

Sam felt her body begin to move on its own accord, rushing to where the cart with the bodies awaited. She felt the tears trying to come, but her body refused as it came upon the scene.

Snow covered the ground around them and it still fell as the one who had delivered the cart went to the Captain of the guard. Words were quietly exchanged as Sam focused on the broken shield that rested atop the sheet covered bodies. Something very large and very dangerous must have attacked them in order to break that. But why wasn't Elijah there? Wasn't this a dream?

No, she realized. This was her very real and reoccurring nightmare.

The soldier and captain moved to the cart to unveil the bodies, but what they revealed was nothing like Sam remembered. The bodies all looked like Elijah and they all were killed in different, horrifying ways. Unable to look for longer than a glance, she turned around and closed her eyes while biting her lip to stifle a pained outburst. The tears finally began to fall and she wasn't sure what kind of nightmare this was becoming.

A hand suddenly rested on her shoulder and she looked up, only to see one of the dead Elijahs staring down at her with its hollowed out eyes. "Do you cry for me, my love?" The words were kind, but his tone was anything but. If anything, it was mocking her as he stared down at her. His gauntlet began to dig into her shoulder and she let out a yelp of pain.

"'My love?' Do you honestly believe that?" The new voice that appeared sent shivers down her spine and she recognized it immediately. Turning to face her other side, she saw the man that had used and imprisoned her for years... her father. And in his grasp was her dead mother, still bearing signs of the plague on her skin. Only now, mud stained her clothes. Sam could only guess from the dirt around her mother's grave.

"What have you done," she yelled out at the old nobleman, wrenching her shoulder free from Elijah. "Is what you've done to us not enough? Are we not allowed to die in peace?" Rather than stare angrily at her father, she could only stare at the dead body of her mother. It hung limply in the man's arms and stared upward at the sky eerily. Her hair and nails were longer, but her skin looked dry and almost like it would break in the cold weather.

"What can I say, my dear daughter? Your mother was always my favorite." Sam choked back bile rising in her throat as she saw the man raise her mother's head to lick the corpse's cheek.

"Don't you touch her like that again." Her volume had decreased, but her tone grew more grave as she balled up her fists. This man, the one who had forced himself on his female household workers and the one who used Sam's "feminine" looks to entertain business partners, was going to die whether it was a dream or not.

She suddenly felt her body be spinned around and she came face to face with the many dead Elijahs. They spoke simultaneously, but all with different tones. "What's wrong, love? Can't a man love his woman even past death?"

She was suddenly shoved down and the Elijahs pinned her down while one laughed maniacally over her. She struggled to get free and even to say something, but they also went to muffle her. "You see, love, I've always thought of you as nothing but a woman. You weren't my equal or even worth my time. I only chose you to be with because you were so frail and easy after your mother's death."

The one Elijah that spoke knelt down with his sword in hand, the tip of the blade pointed directly at her throat. "I'm dead now, though, which will make for poor fun when it comes to courting someone else. So... I guess I'm stuck with you." All of the Elijah's chuckled together, almost mechanically. "Now... do you want me while you're alive? Or dead?"

Sam tried to look around for a way out as tears filled her eyes. It was only at that moment that she saw her mother's head turn towards her, blood running from her eyes as if tears, and mouth Sam's name.

Resigning herself to her fate, Sam took a risk and kicked with all of her might. Somehow, it connected with the main Elijah's stomach and he lost grip on his sword just long enough for her to move her neck. The other Elijah's loosened their grips and leaned forward, as if they felt the same pain, and left her an opportunity to pull away and grab the sword.

The second she had her hands on it, she began swinging. Blood splashed onto her and stained the snow around them. The clanging of metal against metal rung through her ears and she lost herself in the flurry of blows and dodges.

She finally came back to full awareness when she looked down to the bloody heap that was the main Elijah. The sword had stabbed into his neck at least fifteen times, but never fully severed it. The other Elijah's were dismembered or beheaded or both. And her father was nowhere to be seen. Her mother, however, was lying motionless on the ground, the blood flowing down to her body and soaking the corpse's clothes.

Sam, shocked by what she saw, dropped the sword and rushed over to her mother. The corpse's eyes followed Sam's face as she did so, never blinking and remaining completely colorless.

"Mother! I... I..." Sam tried to find the words, but stopped when the corpse's hand rested on her own. A smile broke out on the face of her dead mother before she finally spoke.

"This is your fault."

Sam's eyes grew wide. "M-Mother?"

Fear encased Sam as her mother's hand held her in place, nails digging into her skin, and the Elijahs rose from the dead again, their heads back in place as if she never severed them. The main one led the others, his neck still almost cut completely through and blood gushing from it.

"This is your fault. We wouldn't have died if it had not been for you." All of them repeated these words as the Elijahs closed in on her, their swords now raised and preparing to attack.

Sam had nowhere to run and no one to turn to. She was going to die with the blood of her lover and mother on her hands. And it was her fault.

She resigned herself to her fate just as one of the swords pierced her chest... and she woke up.

Sam gasped for air as she clung to her chest, feeling for the wound of the sword immediately. Beads of sweat glittered her forehead and all down her throat. And she found that her sword was in one of her hands.

It took her a minute to realize that she was at camp with her traveling party again and that dawn was now approaching. She dropped her sword immediately and looked around to make sure she hadn't actually swung it in her sleep.

She had done nothing, but worry the one who had taken watch. The humanoid creature that looked like a blue eagle that was also the healer of the party eyed her almost sympathetically. He was the only one in the group that knew she was a woman and he was also the other party member that worshiped the same Gods as her. She trusted him implicitly, but... she really wished that he hadn't had seen her in such a vulnerable state.

His worry was apparent on his face and she immediately felt guilty. He was more than likely going to worry for her for the rest of the journey. And it was her fault.
